pr_body:
For a particular document distribution (each of the three documents matching the boolean query
live in separate leave readers) we calculate the hit count without actually collecting. 
TotalHitCountCollector#getLeafCollector throws a CollectionTerminatedException(), which again shortcuts the PartialHitCountsCollectors collect() method to be called at all.
It should happen very rarely, and in that case we can check if the reason for not triggering the early termination
was that we can get the document count from the term statistics. Thats what this change proposes

Closes #97359
pr_comments: @javanna pushed the simplifications by creating a non-early-terminating TermQuery.

@javanna thanks for the review, I added the same treatment for QueryPhaseTests#testTerminateAfterSize0NoHitCountShortcut using the modified TermsQuery from the other test as well. It did have the same problems when running it often enough.

comments:
The error only seems to happen for a particular document distribution. I currently believe that in the failing case, each of the three documents matching the boolean live in separate leave readers (more unlikely than having more than one doc in one leave with this setup). In that case, upon creating the initial Weight, BooleanWeight#optCount seems to be able to calculate the weight without running the actual query. This is why TotalHitCountCollector#getLeafCollector throws a CollectionTerminatedException(), which again shortcuts the PartialHitCountsCollectors collect() method to be called at all.
I yet have to verify if my theory makes sense and how / if we need to remedy this.
